Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KXrn3t8p6XTbLM1U9HS53a
* Pick kanji-quiz distractors by shape so the answer isn't guessable
The kanji quiz drew its 3 wrong readings at random, which let the answer be found without reading the kanji at all: 売れる against れんしゅう/ げんき/いちど is settled by the trailing れる alone.
pickReadingDistractors() now prefers readings that survive that shortcut — same okurigana tail first, then a similar mora count, then the same opening mora, shuffling before the sort so equally-good candidates still vary. Measured over the current 107 entries, that cuts "answerable from the okurigana tail alone" from 24% to 8% and "answerable from length alone" from 43% to 1%. 起きる now reads およぐ / おくる / おもい / おきる instead of a mix of unrelated shapes.
It also dedupes by reading. Preferring similar readings makes homophones prime candidates, and two entries sharing a reading would have rendered the same choice twice — kanji.json has no such pair yet, but the list grows daily and Japanese supplies plenty.
vocab/listening keep the random picker: those quizzes ask for the meaning, where shape similarity doesn't apply.
test/smoke.js now checks the kanji round offers 4 distinct choices that are all real readings from the data, which is what the dedupe and the scoring could plausibly break.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KXrn3t8p6XTbLM1U9HS53a
* Use the aspirated hangul forms for か행/た행 kana
The owner spotted that the kana quiz answered か with 가 and asked whether 카 isn't the accurate reading. Both had a basis — 가 is the 외래어 표기법's 어두 form, 카 its 어중·어말 form — but 카 is the better fit here, so か/き/く/け/こ and た/ち/て/と now use 카키쿠케코/타치테토 in both kana files. つ stays 쓰: the 표기법 gives it 쓰 in either position.
Why the switch:
- A lone kana has no word position, so applying the 어두 rule to it was already an arbitrary pick rather than the standard being honoured. - Japanese word-initial voiceless stops fall between Korean 예사소리 and 거센소리; the 1986 committee called them closer to 예사소리 and that reading is still contested. - Decisive: the 어두 form collides with dakuten. か=가 and が=가, た=다 and だ=다, ち=지 and ぢ=지 — the quiz would stop working the moment が행 is added. The aspirated form keeps every pair distinct.
CLAUDE.md said the opposite, so it's rewritten with the reasoning to stop a future session "correcting" it back. It also now records that お/を share 오 legitimately (を really is /o/), and that pickDistractors doesn't dedupe, so a future duplicate hangul value would show the same choice twice in the kana quiz.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KXrn3t8p6XTbLM1U9HS53a
* Let the kanji quiz reveal a reading on tap, without it counting as recall
Tapping the word (or the cue line under it) swaps #quiz-reveal from "글자를 누르면 읽는 법" to the reading, for kanji that are simply unreadable — looking it up and learning it beats guessing blind.
The reading is the answer in this quiz, so the peek isn't free: quiz.peeked makes selectAnswer record the item as not recalled even when the chosen answer is right, keeping it in the wrong-answer review queue. Otherwise peeking would clear precisely the words that still need drilling, quietly undermining the feature that resurfaces them.
Only the kanji quiz wires this up — verified in a browser that the line stays hidden for vocab/hiragana/grammar/listening. renderQuestion resets the element, both handlers and quiz.peeked per question. The new CSS sets no `display`, so the [hidden] attribute keeps working and this can't repeat the .quiz-replay bug.
Tests cover the cue text, that tapping shows the current item's reading, and that a peeked-then-answered-correctly kanji is still queued for review.

* Use the aspirated hangul forms for か행/た행 kana

The owner spotted that the kana quiz answered か with 가 and asked
whether 카 isn't the accurate reading. Both had a basis — 가 is the
외래어 표기법's 어두 form, 카 its 어중·어말 form — but 카 is the better
fit here, so か/き/く/け/こ and た/ち/て/と now use 카키쿠케코/타치테토 in
both kana files. つ stays 쓰: the 표기법 gives it 쓰 in either position.

Why the switch:

- A lone kana has no word position, so applying the 어두 rule to it was
  already an arbitrary pick rather than the standard being honoured.
- Japanese word-initial voiceless stops fall between Korean 예사소리 and
  거센소리; the 1986 committee called them closer to 예사소리 and that
  reading is still contested.
- Decisive: the 어두 form collides with dakuten. か=가 and が=가, た=다
  and だ=다, ち=지 and ぢ=지 — the quiz would stop working the moment
  が행 is added. The aspirated form keeps every pair distinct.

CLAUDE.md said the opposite, so it's rewritten with the reasoning to
stop a future session "correcting" it back. It also now records that
お/を share 오 legitimately (を really is /o/), and that pickDistractors
doesn't dedupe, so a future duplicate hangul value would show the same
choice twice in the kana quiz.

be found without reading the kanji at all: 売れる against れんしゅう/
げんき/いちど is settled by the trailing れる alone.

the same opening mora, shuffling before the sort so equally-good
candidates still vary. Measured over the current 107 entries, that cuts
"answerable from the okurigana tail alone" from 24% to 8% and
"answerable from length alone" from 43% to 1%. 起きる now reads

prime candidates, and two entries sharing a reading would have rendered
the same choice twice — kanji.json has no such pair yet, but the list
grows daily and Japanese supplies plenty.

meaning, where shape similarity doesn't apply.

are all real readings from the data, which is what the dedupe and the
scoring could plausibly break.
